How i prepared for Leadership Questions (Behaviourval Questions) asked for Amazon.
During Amazon interview , you will come across question on Leadership Principles in each round and this is really important to get into Amazon.
So don't neglect this if you get chance to interview with Amazon.
HR had told me to answer all Leadership Questions (Behaviourval) using ‘STAR’ pattern.
S(Situation): Describe the SITUATION you were in.
T(task): Explain the TASK that needed to be done.
A(Action): Detail the ACTION that you took to achieve the task.
R(Result): Reveal the RESULTS of your action.
How to answer in better way:
1) Give all answer using STAR pattern.
2) Give answer relating to your work experience / projects using technical terms to get good impression rather than giving general answer.
Note: I gave very generalised answer in 1st round and feedback was mixed for behavioural question.
What all questions i have prepared?
-> I just researched for few hours and went through a more than 20+ recent interview experiences on Leetcode and noted all unique Leadership questions(behavioural) at once place.
-> Prepared for each question using STAR pattern relating to my experience with different different technical terms.
-> For 1-2 questions that i was not able to relate to my experiences in better way, i took help of chatgpt to frame a better answer.
Note: I encountered most of the exact questions that I had researched and collected. I am sharing a Google Doc link where I noted these questions with two youtube video link inside this.
Google Doc link: https://lnkd.in/gJtmF7YP
Note: I really liked this “STAR’ technique and we can use in other companies as well to answer behavioral questions.
Before my Amazon interview, I used to be very scared of behavioral questions. However, after the interview, I am no longer afraid of them and feel much more confident.
Keep coding, Keep applying!!

ai_analysis.summary: This is a personal account of preparing for Amazon Leadership Principle and behavioral questions rather than a data engineering technical post. The author recommends using the STAR pattern—Situation, Task, Action, and Result—and connecting answers to real work experience and projects with relevant technical terminology rather than giving only a generalized response. The author reports reviewing more than 20 recent interview experiences on Leetcode, preparing answers to the collected questions, and using ChatGPT to frame answers for one or two questions that did not relate well to their experience. The supplied content does not include the individual questions from the linked document.
subtopics: tailoring answers to technical work and projects

interview_questions.question: How should a candidate structure an answer to an Amazon behavioral or Leadership Principle question?
interview_questions.answer:
The answer should describe the Situation, Task, Action, and Result.
The candidate should use a relevant work experience or project and explain the result of the action taken.

interview_questions.question: Why can a generalized behavioral answer be weak, and how can technical project experience improve it?
interview_questions.answer:
The author received mixed behavioral feedback after giving a generalized response in the first round.
A stronger response can connect the answer to the candidate's own work or projects and use relevant technical terminology.

interview_questions.question: How can a candidate prepare for behavioral and leadership questions before an Amazon interview?
interview_questions.answer:
The candidate can review recent interview experiences and collect recurring leadership questions.
Each question can be prepared with the STAR pattern and linked to genuine work experience or projects using technical terminology.
The post reports using ChatGPT to help frame answers for one or two questions that did not relate well to the candidate's experience.
